content_md:
Seems directionally right that true AI use is dynamic, embodied, alive, motion-full. Reminds me of an idea that those who excel at abstract thought aren’t really thinking abstractly; they’ve just learned to concretise and embody the abstractness somehow or somewhere. This seems like that.

> This brings us to AI. AI is like riding a powered two-wheeler, like a motorcycle or scooter. Some people who learn to ride a bike never go on to learn to ride powered two-wheelers. You need excess regulatory capacity to manage the greater mass and velocity. This is harder than either riding a bike or driving a car.
